facts.fact: Rome developed from huts into a city, then a republic with overseas territories.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Roman Republic
facts.note: The closing is an editorial reflection on ordinary life, not an additional dated event.

facts.fact: The late republic suffered prolonged civil wars before Octavian secured control.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Roman Republic

facts.fact: Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium before annexing Egypt.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Roman Egypt

facts.fact: The Senate granted Octavian the title Augustus in twenty seven years before Christ.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Roman Empire

facts.fact: Augustus preserved republican forms while exercising autocratic power.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Roman Art: A Resource for Educators

facts.fact: The Senate continued meeting but lost initiative in foreign and military affairs.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Roman Art: A Resource for Educators

facts.fact: Egypt supplied the city of Rome with grain after its conquest.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Roman Egypt

facts.fact: Later emperors extended Roman frontiers and developed imperial administration.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Roman Empire

facts.fact: Rome governed Egypt through a prefect, Roman law, and military garrisons.
facts.source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Roman Egypt
facts.note: Scene seven generalizes these documented mechanisms; the closing is an editorial reflection.
